BACKPORT: drm/i915: initialize backlight max from VBT Normally we determine the backlight PWM modulation frequency (which we also use as backlight max value) from the backlight registers at module load time, expecting the registers have been initialized by the BIOS. If this is not the case, we fail. The VBT contains the backlight modulation frequency in Hz. Add platform specific functions to convert the frequency in Hz to backlight PWM modulation frequency, and use them to initialize the backlight when the registers are not initialized by the BIOS. v2: Fix SPT and VLV. Thanks to Clint for the VLV code. Cc: Clint Taylor <clinton.a.taylor@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Clint Taylor <Clinton.A.Taylor@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Conflicts: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_panel.c (minor context change, initialize backlight_hz_to_pwm for vlv as well to resolve compiler warning) BUG=chrome-os-partner:43071 TEST=Enable normal mode - /usr/share/vboot/bin/set_gbb_flags.sh 0x0 Change-Id: I13539f8ce4a72d87d1ab3f675615974f8f2d8d2a Link: git://anongit.freedesktop.org/drm-intel ref:drm-intel-next (cherry picked from commit aa17cdb4f8367875d3a53c41e004fc02e983e317) Signed-off-by: Shobhit Kumar <shobhit.kumar@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/308579 Tested-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Joe Konno <joe.konno@linux.intel.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: James Ausmus <james.ausmus@intel.com>

BACKPORT: drm/i915/skl: If needed sanitize bios programmed cdclk Especially in cases where pre-os does not enable display, cdclk might not be in sane state. During sanitization initialize cdclk with maximum value till we get dynamic cdclk support. v2: Check if BIOS programmed correctly rather than always calling init - Do validation of programmed cdctl and what it is expected - Only do slk_init_cdclk if validation failed else reuse BIOS programmed value v3: Move the validation logic in a separate sanitize function (Ville) v4: No need to check LCPLL after sanitize and use max_cdclk_freq instead of hardcoded value (Ville) Cc: Imre Deak <imre.deak@intel.com> Cc: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Shobhit Kumar <shobhit.kumar@intel.com> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1445344992-14658-1-git-send-email-shobhit.kumar@intel.com Reviewed-by: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Daniel Vetter <daniel.vetter@ffwll.ch> Conflicts: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/intel_display.c (minor context change) BUG=chrome-os-partner:43071 TEST=Enable normal mode - /usr/share/vboot/bin/set_gbb_flags.sh 0x0 Change-Id: Ic5179e2a77149dd7fb899312cbcf1f6d88a0a168 Link: git://anongit.freedesktop.org/drm-intel ref:drm-intel-next-queued (cherry picked from commit c73666f394fca498978f71e66062eb3e3f2c7951) Signed-off-by: Shobhit Kumar <shobhit.kumar@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/308750 Tested-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Joe Konno <joe.konno@linux.intel.com> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: James Ausmus <james.ausmus@intel.com>

BACKPORT: drm/i915/skl: While sanitizing cdclock check the SWF18 as well SWF18 is set if the display has been initialized by the pre-os. It also gives what configuration is enabled on which pipe. In skl_sanitize_cdclk, the DPLL sanity check can pass even if GOP/VBIOS is not loaded as BIOS enables DPLL for integrated audio codec related programming. So fisrt check if SWF18 is set and then follow through with other DPLL and CDCLK verification. If not set then for sure we need to sanitize the cdclock. v2: Update the commit message for clarity (Siva) v3: Correct the mask to check for bits[23:0] instead of only bits[16:0]. Had missed checking for PIPE C altogether. Remaining are reserved (Siva) v4: Use ILK_SWF macro for SWF register definitions. Taken from Ville's patch http://lists.freedesktop.org/archives/intel-gfx/2015-November/079480.html Cc: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Signed-off-by: Shobhit Kumar <shobhit.kumar@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Sivakumar Thulasimani <sivakumar.thulasimani@intel.com> Acked-by: Ville Syrjl <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com> Link: http://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/1446726932-14078-1-git-send-email-shobhit.kumar@intel.com Signed-off-by: Jani Nikula <jani.nikula@intel.com> Conflicts: drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_reg.h (minor context change) BUG=chrome-os-partner:43071 TEST=Enable normal mode - /usr/share/vboot/bin/set_gbb_flags.sh 0x0 Change-Id: I349af0381ac56f69aca5f5bb944e45fc9829be45 Link: git://anongit.freedesktop.org/drm-intel ref:drm-intel-next-queued (cherry picked from commit f1b391a55134df0d338a6ff829baa0f578d86852) Signed-off-by: Shobhit Kumar <shobhit.kumar@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/311112 Tested-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Stéphane Marchesin <marcheu@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: James Ausmus <james.ausmus@intel.com>

CHROMIUM: usb: gadget: tegra_xudc: Don't poll for port reset completion Quickcharge chargers are generating Port Reset Change (PRC) events upon connection which never complete. Since the XUDC appears to generate PRC events on both 1-to-0 and 0-to-1 transitions of the Port Reset (PR) bit, we can avoid polling for completion of the port reset by ignoring the 0-to-1 transition. The port reset will then be handled on the PRC event generated by the 1-to-0 transition. Do the same for WRC/WPR to avoid a similar situation there. BUG=b:25699970 TEST=Connecting a QC2.0 charger to Smaug no longer hangs the system. ADB, MTP, etc. still work. Change-Id: Ie059f827b8ff4675ff69148bc63358c8a5476c78 Signed-off-by: Andrew Bresticker <abrestic@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/312866 Reviewed-by: Jim Lin <jilin@nvidia.com> Reviewed-by: Vincent Palatin <vpalatin@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: mmc: sdhci-pxav3: enable modifying MMC_CARD bit during card initialization On Marvell Armada 38x SoC's the MMC_CARD bit in SD_CE_ATA_1 register must be set to 0x1 when a MMC card is supposed to work in DDR mode, or when commands CMD11, CMD14 and CMD20 are used. This commit enables the above for all MMC cards by modifying the host registers during card initialization. It is done by using init_card callback.
